predecessors.name: Roman Republic
predecessors.text: Hispania outside the Pyrenean coast and the lower Baetis

successors.name: Roman Republic
successors.text: Hispania outside the Pyrenean coast and the lower Baetis

ledger.x: 80 BC: Sertorius 'landed at Baelo in 80 BC' after 'Lusitanian envoys had invited him to lead them'; he 'first organized the Lusitanian tribes before returning to the Baetis valley', presenting himself as proconsul and 'the legitimate Roman governor of Hispania'.
80-72 BC: the Sertorian War ('80-72 BC'); Metellus Pius 'Entered Spain in late 80 or early 79 BC and was repeatedly outmaneuvered'.

77 BC: 'most of the Iberia Peninsula' after 'consolidating both Hispania Ulterior and Citerior between 80 and 77 BC'; Osca his capital; Metellus and Pompey keep 'parts of the Baetis line and the Pyrenean coast'.
76-75 BC: Pompey's eastern campaign: Lauron (76), Valentia, Sucro and Saguntum (75).
75 BC: the coastal battles end; 74-73 in the Ebro valley (Palentia, Calagurris).

72 BC: Perperna 'assassinated Sertorius during a banquet' ('normally assumed' 72; Spann argues 73); Pompey 'ambushed Perperna's army, executed Perperna and the assassins, and burned Sertorius's papers'.
72 BC: the faction state ends; 'Many supporters received citizenship, and a group of fanatical opponents was resettled at Lugdunum Convenarum'.

certainty.note: A civil-war faction's territory: 'most of the Iberia Peninsula' at the height (77) with the Sullan 'parts of the Baetis line and the Pyrenean coast' excluded; the shifting front of 76-73 is not drawn year by year.
